rounds.summary: Fixed the broken order form — the submit handler targeted a nonexistent `orderform` id so every order silently failed; it now wires to the real `#order-form`, validates the two required fields, and confirms inline via the existing `#order-status` element, turning the site's only conversion path back on.

Made the page — and above all the order form — actually usable on a 375px phone by replacing the fixed 980px layout with a real viewport and fluid, touch-friendly form controls (16px inputs to stop iOS zoom, full-width tap-target submit button), and swapped out the banned Comic Sans/marquee for a clean font and a static promo bar that keeps the muffin offer visible.
Replaced the free-text "Drink" field with a priced, menu-matched radio picker (coffee pre-selected, big tap targets) so customers order in one tap with no typos — fewer abandoned or wrong orders.

Added a one-tap "Add a muffin" add-on to the order form (making the promo bar's 50¢-off offer actually orderable for the first time) plus a live order total above the button, so the form upsells at checkout and customers see the exact price before committing.

Added a sticky mobile-only "Order now" bar that keeps the order form one tap away at all times on phones (auto-hiding when the form is on screen), so scrolling customers never lose the conversion action.
Turned the dead-text menu into a tappable menu where each row pre-selects that item in the order form and jumps straight to it, so browsing the menu converts into an order in one tap.

Added an above-the-fold hero CTA ("Order ahead — skip the line") with a reassurance line under the header, so the first screen ends in an order action instead of only text, matching the submit button's styling for consistency.

Replaced the easy-to-miss one-line post-submit blip with a loud receipt-style confirmation panel (order summary, total, and a concrete "ready around 3:45 PM" time) and flipped the submit button to "Place another order", so success is unmistakable, double-submits don't happen, and the loop invites a second item.

Added a "Most popular" badge to the big coffee and made it the preselected default in the order form, so social proof plus a ready-made choice steers first-time buyers to the house favorite instead of stalling on an open decision.

Added a "How many drinks?" quantity select inside the drink picker so one order can cover two or more drinks — bigger average tickets, and couples/coworkers no longer hit a dead-end forcing them to submit twice.

Added a one-tap "Your usual" reorder button at the top of the order form — the last placed order is saved locally and returning customers refill the entire form (drink, size, qty, muffin, name) with one tap and land on the submit button, turning a repeat order into two taps instead of re-typing everything.

Made the name field — the only thing a customer has to type before ORDER NOW — zero-effort and self-recovering: phones can autofill it in one tap via autocomplete="name", a placeholder explains why we ask, and native required validation stops an empty name right at the field with focus and a message instead of letting the order stall.
